findings.title: Reject native directory traversal errors before qualifying a complete inventory
findings.evidence: os.walk(root, followlinks=False) omits its onerror callback. A deterministic os.scandir PermissionError for a real child containing a real file was silently swallowed. The hidden file was modified between inventories; both returned successfully and before == after, with the hidden file absent from both inventories.
findings.impact: The all-native-file preservation claim can qualify a partial inventory, so a loss or change inside an unreadable subtree is not detected.
findings.requested_correction: Make directory enumeration errors fail closed and add a focused negative control proving an unreadable child cannot produce a qualifying inventory.

findings.title: Reserve the new controlled-install phase in the Properties batch time budget
findings.evidence: minimum_lane_budget remains 1380s for properties-set, unchanged from the old path. The new phase has six query calls bounded at 30s, four ps observations at 30s, two inventory scans guarded at 120s, and one 120s install: 660s of additional declared operation bounds before code hashing and local validation.
findings.impact: The batch can start Properties with enough time for the old profile but insufficient time for its now-required controlled install and native postflight, causing a worker deadline failure instead of NOT_RUN_BUDGET. Existing 180s general overhead does not account for this new phase.
findings.requested_correction: Give the whole controlled-install phase an explicit bounded budget, include it only in the Properties minimum lane budget, and add a near-deadline negative control. Preserve worker/cleanup deadlines and mandatory postflight.

positive_findings: Original account, Space, subject, preparation PID, source/run/attempt/nonce, baseline and fixture hashes remain bound through installation and native postflight.
Exactly one controlled same-build install is used; failures/cancellation have no fallback or account reconstruction.

Python compares its exact directory identities before and after its own phases. Foundation captures actual native entry identities and compares its own complete identities exactly during restoration and readback; no cross-library numeric tolerance was introduced.

The native state comparison changes only the directory pair after the proved install. Original canonical bytes and association IDs/timestamps, Type, complete Tag/link/backlink sets and seeded block identities remain exact.
Saved batch qualification requires the new installation hash and schema-2 native receipt; legacy receipt cannot qualify.
Application product source, native semantic read methods, Kit pins, UI assertions and method selection were not changed.
